MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 13, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 7:10 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Sheriff Captain Kimberly Guerrero.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Donald Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING FEBRUARY 2024 AS BLACK HISTORY MONTH

MAYOR SCHMITZ declared February 2024 as Black History Month.

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING FEBRUARY 2024 AS AMERICAN HEART MONTH

MAYOR SCHMITZ declared February 2024 as American Heart Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

Assistant City Manager Davis read Resolutions 2564 & 2565 by title.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF
  FREE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE -FIRST QUARTER
  2024 + PRESENTATION ON SUN VALLEY RECYCLING CENTER

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 76 CYPRESS WAY
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: JP MORGAN CHASE

Waste Management representative Erick Quintero provided an overview of the City’s waste
collection data and of the recycling process at the Sun Valley Recycling Center.

Los Angeles County Sheriff Captain Kimberly Guerrero introduced Deputy Page to the City
Council and community.

Public comment was received from Merlin David from the Peninsula Friends of the Library
announcing a Black Heritage event to be held at Peninsula Center Library from 11:00 am –
1:00 pm on February 17, 2024.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 13, 2024
 Public comment was also received from Brandee Kieth from the South Coast AQMD inviting
residents and businesses to take part in their Electric Lawn and Garden programs.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN
  THE CITIES OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, RANCHO PALOS VERDES, ROLLING
  HILLS, AND ROLLING HILLS ESTATES RELATING TO THE PLACEMENT AND
  MAINTENANCE OF AUTOMATED LICENSE PLATE RECOGNITION CAMERAS
  AROUND THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the First Amendment to the
  Memorandum of Understanding between the cities of Palos Verdes Estates, Rancho
  Palos Verdes, Rolling Hills and Rolling Hills Estates for the replacement purchase
  and installation of the Regional Automatic License Plate Recognition Camera system,
  approved as to form by the City Attorney.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Discussion ensued about the lifespan of the camera equipment and the need for replacement
seven years after installation.

LASD Captain Guerrero emphasized the importance of the technology being compatible with
that of the Sheriff’s Department, and the importance of the ALPR cameras for not only stolen
vehicles, but for amber alerts.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA stated that in the future, if there is another technology
compatible with the LASD data retention policies and capabilities, staff should consider
upgrading to a less expensive and equally effective option.

MAYOR SCHMITZ shared the discussion held during the Peninsula Public Safety meeting
about the consideration of this MOU amendment. She emphasized that it was very well vetted
by staff and the entire Committee, and that this is a culmination of many months of work.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITIES OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  RANCHO PALOS VERDES, ROLLING HILLS AND ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  FOR THE REPLACEMENT PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF THE
  REGIONAL AUTOMATIC LICENSE PLATE RECOGNITION CAMERA
  SYSTEM, APPROVED AS TO FORM BY THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 240054
  DETERMINATION THAT UNLISTED USE OF VIRTUAL REALITY ELECTRONIC
  SPORTS AND GAMES IS SIMILAR TO AND NOT MORE OBJECTIONABLE THAN
  USES ALREADY LISTED IN SECTION 17.04.030 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE
  LOCATION: 550 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE, UNIT 139

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the issues and adopt Resolution No.
  2566, determining that a Virtual Reality Esports business is similar to and not more

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 13, 2024
   objectionable than other service uses already listed in RHEMC Section 17.30.020,
  and determining that in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act
  (Public Resources Code § 21000 et seq.: “CEQA”), the application is Categorically
  Exempt under Class 1, Section 15301 Existing Facilities.

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA made note of the letter received by the City from the Palos
Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce in support of opening this new business.

The applicant explained the hours of operation are planned to be 12:00 pm to 8:00 pm, and
possibly until 9:00 pm on Fridays and Saturdays, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM
STEGURA. He also noted the target age group for this business is 6 – 12-year-olds.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2566, DETERMINING THAT A VIRTUAL REALITY
  ESPORTS BUSINESS IS SIMILAR TO AND NOT MORE OBJECTIONABLE
  THAN OTHER SERVICE USES ALREADY LISTED IN RHEMC SECTION
  17.30.020, AND DETERMINING THAT IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE
  CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (PUBLIC RESOURCES
  CODE § 21000 ET SEQ.: “CEQA”), THE APPLICATION IS CATEGORICALLY
  EXEMPT UNDER CLASS 1, SECTION 15301 EXISTING FACILITIES.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

Assistant City Manager Davis read Resolution No. 2566 by title.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Neighborhood Council meeting, as well as the
CalCOG Annual Conference in Monterey last week.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER noted that the Traffic & Safety Committee will meet next
week, and highlighted the discussions held during the last Equestrian Committee meeting.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA stated that she, along with MAYOR SCHMITZ AND
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER, attended the Jan Ball plaque dedication ceremony at
Peter Weber Equestrian Center and the Carol Dean Porter plaque dedication ceremony at
Ernie Howlett Park this week. She also attended the South Bay Cities Council of
Governments (SBCCOG) Board of Directors meeting last month.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked City staff, specifically the Maintenance crew for their hard work
during the heavy rains last week.

At 8:03 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting in memory of Malcolm Sharp, Carol
